title: Audioengine Made a Kit for You, and It Was All Yellow
gist: A 7/10 WIRED review of Audioengine's 2026 yellow Color of the Year kit (A2+ Gen 3 speakers, S6 subwoofer, Crosley C6 Bluetooth turntable, stands), priced around $857-866 with no bundle discount. The reviewer praises design cohesion, easy setup and sound for the size, with the turntable the weak link.

insights.claim: Audioengine releases an annual Color of the Year home audio kit: matte blue in 2024, metallic green in 2025 and egg-yolk yellow in 2026.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Limited-color bundles are a differentiation tactic in a category dominated by black, silver and wood grain.

insights.claim: The 2026 kit costs about $857 to $866 and bundling gives no price break versus buying the components individually.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: The premium is for color matching, not savings.
insights.quote: (If you don't want the entire suite, you can buy the components à la carte without a penalty—there's no price break for the bundled suite.)

insights.claim: The 2026 kit adds a color-matched Bluetooth turntable, the C6, made in collaboration with Crosley, with a steel platter, MDF plinth, two speeds and built-in preamp.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Partnerships extend the lineup into vinyl-adjacent entry-level products.

insights.claim: The reviewer calls the price incredibly competitive across the entry-level home stereo space.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Positions the kit as value-for-design at the entry level.

insights.claim: The compact A2+ Gen 3 speakers, 6 inches by 4 inches, offer mini-jack, USB and RCA inputs plus RCA outputs and can power a small home theater, working for hi-fi, gaming and laptops.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Multi-input versatility broadens the use cases of small powered speakers.

insights.claim: The S6 powered subwoofer is a compact class D front-firing unit with response down to 33 Hz and adjustable crossover, and it tracks speaker volume in lockstep once connected.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Small-form-factor bass is a key reason the kit suits tight spaces.

insights.claim: Setup is simple: Bluetooth pairing, RCA connection for the subwoofer and QR codes that launch step-by-step setup guides make it intuitive for novices.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Ease of setup lowers the barrier for novice buyers.

insights.claim: The turntable is the weak link: its aluminum tonearm falls short for higher-end users, but swapping in a Sony PS-LX3BT produced no significant sound difference.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Competing turntables match sound, so aesthetic unity is the main competitive edge.

insights.claim: The main thing similar Bluetooth turntables lack is the aesthetic unity of a fully color-matched system.
insights.speaker: Jordan Michelman
insights.so_what: Design cohesion is what is being monetized.
